messages:
elaine: Heads up — customers hitting /console/insights now sometimes see rows from other orgs after the canary rolled this morning. Not widespread but reproducible with quick org-switches.

sam: omg, saw one email. can you repro reliably? steps? :eyes:

elaine: yes, repro steps: 1) open org A dashboard, 2) quick-switch to org B (top-left), 3) expand 'recent queries' panel, some cards show org A ids.

marta: that sounds like a prefetch/kv cache mismatch between the route that renders the list and the route that expands details. maybe header not propagated?

ryan: which headers are we using for tenant routing now? X-Org-ID in edge header + session cookie, right?

elaine: right. stack: router -> prefetch service -> console rendering. logs show requests to /api/insights/prefetch with X-Org-ID=B but the backend served cached payload keyed by the prefetch key which didn't include org id.

sam: so cache key missing org qualifier. that would match a lot of prior leaks. is the prefetch service owned by eng-platform or eng-runtime?

marta: eng-platform but we had an earlier refactor to move key construction to a shared internal-api. suspect the shared lib changed to use user.id instead of org.id for some endpoints.

elaine: here's a snippet from the prefeth call trace:```
GET /prefetch?panel=recent_queries
Headers:
  Cookie: session=abc
  X-Org-ID: B
CacheKey: prefetch:recent_queries:session:abc  # missing org id
```

ryan: ugh. that key is definitely wrong. we need org in key. owners? @marta, can you check the shared lib change?

marta: on it. quick grep shows change in internal-api v3.4.2: keyBuilder now uses request.user.id when session cookie present. patch looks like:```
- keyParts.push(req.user.orgId)
+ keyParts.push(req.user.id)
```

sam: is that a deliberate behavioral change? who approved that?

marta: not deliberate for prefetch. looks like someone added a generic optimization for per-user caching and didn't think about multi-tenant panels.

elaine: impact: dashboards that combine cross-tenant and per-user panels may mix org-scoped and user-scoped caches. customers with fast switching hit stale org-blended payloads.

ryan: mitigation options: 1) revert internal-api change (fast), 2) add org qualifier at prefetch callsite (slower), 3) emergency rollback of canary (if needed).

marta: i can open a PR to revert the keyBuilder line and add tests for org-specific cache keys. take ~30m.

sam: can we do a canary rollback in the console rollout UI? deploy-bot, status of canary?

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-21T09:10:12Z canary=console-rollout-v2 fraction=20% health=green id=deploy-7821

elaine: health shows green but that's not catching this because it's low-signal. we should pause the canary and rollback the internal-api change instead.

ryan: agree. pause canary now and revert internal-api. @marta file the PR and tag me; i'll approve and merge + trigger private rollout. also file an alert rule to catch org-keyed cache hits mixing orgs.

marta: PR opened: internal-api#489; added test coverage for cache key includes orgId when endpoint is org-scoped. also added a note in API docs about per-user vs per-org cache semantics.

sam: small ask for telemetry/observability: can we add a quick gauge that counts prefetch cache hits where response.orgId != request.orgId? we can emit an anomaly when >0.

ryan: good idea. we can add a trace enrichment in prefetch service that tags resp_org and req_org and a meter for mismatch_count. eng-sre: please add a PagerDuty rule if mismatch_count spikes above 1 for >1m in prod.

elaine: after revert and canary pause, i ran manual tests and cannot repro. i'll follow up with the affected customers.

marta: deploying revert now. ETA 12m. will post updates.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-21T09:22:34Z canary paused id=deploy-7821 action=paused

ryan: thanks. after this we should review rollout UX: make it easier to flag low-signal but severity-high regressions (privacy). maybe an option on the console to run a tenant-isolation smoke test during canary.

sam: +1. this bug is privacy-sensitive; even low replication rate is unacceptable. add to postmortem checklist. :exclamation:

elaine: agreed. filing a short blameless postmortem and remediation steps. will include required unit tests and a telemetry rule.

marta: revert merged and promoted to canary-free environments. leaving follow-up TODOs: add cache key linting, add tenant-isolation smoke job in rollout pipeline, docs update.

ryan: awesome. appreciate the quick triage.

elaine: thanks everyone. i'll DM the affected customers and keep this thread updated with any new findings.
